_notes: Copy this file to database-bounce.json.
This is the only operation in this reference that changes something on the
database node itself. The OCI API can start and stop a PDB, and it can
restart a whole DB node, but it has no operation that restarts a container
database, so the change is made with dbaascli over SSH. Identity resolution
and the evidence gate are unchanged: verify reads the result back from OCI.
Host access: the node itself is discovered from OCI facts, so only
credentials are declared here. Keep the private key outside this repository.
How the runner reaches the node. A VM Cluster subnet normally forbids public
IPs, so pick one of three:
1. Direct. The runner is already inside the VCN, or routed to it. Leave both
bastion values empty, as set below.
2. Your own jump host: set exacs_bounce_bastion_address to its address and
exacs_bounce_bastion_user to the SSH user on it.
3. OCI Bastion service: create an SSH port forwarding session first, then
set exacs_bounce_bastion_address to the regional session endpoint (for
example host.bastion.uk-london-1.oci.oraclecloud.com) and
exacs_bounce_bastion_user to the session OCID. A managed SSH session will
not do: it needs Oracle Cloud Agent on the target, and a VM Cluster node
is not a compute instance that runs it. The session is bound to one
address and port, so target the node this operation resolves, port 22,
or the bastion refuses the connection.
